requirements.text: A support analyst can chat with an assistant that answers product questions from the organization's product knowledge.
Assistant answers must be grounded in the ingested product-knowledge documents supplied at intake (documents_dir), not in unsourced model knowledge.
The assistant must identify itself clearly as automated so customers know the reply was machine-generated.
The assistant must reference the knowledge sources used for an answer so the reviewing analyst can verify it before approving.
When the knowledge corpus does not cover a question, the assistant must say so and defer to the analyst rather than answer speculatively.
Each incoming support question is routed to the assistant first to produce a draft reply.
An analyst must explicitly approve a draft reply (with the option to edit or reject it) before it is sent; no reply leaves the system unapproved.
Analysts can review past conversations and reuse good answers from them.
The app provides a chat screen where an analyst composes a question and reads the assistant's answer in a turn-by-turn thread.
The app provides a conversation-history screen listing past conversations that can be opened, read, and copied from for reuse.
The draft reply is presented in the UI with explicit approve / edit / reject controls and a visible approval status on each conversation.
Conversation records must be stored so that they are available for quality review.
Stored conversation history must be reviewable through the application, not merely retained in storage.
Persist conversations and their individual messages with timestamps and author role (analyst / assistant) so threads can be reconstructed in order.
Persist the approval decision for each drafted reply (approver, decision, timestamp, whether the text was edited) as the audit trail for quality review.
Persist the knowledge documents ingested from the documents directory and the source references cited by each assistant answer.
Conversation records contain customer support content and must be readable only by support analysts using the application, never exposed anonymously.
The application must run on the local deploy target as a self-contained stack, with no dependency on managed cloud services.
How analysts authenticate and whether analyst identity is recorded on approvals is unspecified.
Retention and handling of stored conversation records (how long they are kept, whether customer PII must be redacted) is unspecified.
Whether the application itself delivers the approved reply to the customer (e.g. outbound email or ticket integration) or the analyst copies it into the existing email tool is unspecified.
